sections.title: Tree and pods
sections.text: Kassod tree is an evergreen tropical tree with a dense, rounded crown, growing to about 20 m. Its pinnate leaves bear many paired leaflets; clusters of yellow flowers are followed by long, flat pods, about 15–30 cm long.

sections.title: Food and toxicity
sections.text: Leaves, flowers and young pods are traditionally eaten in some Southeast Asian dishes, usually after preparation. This does not make every plant part safe: the tree contains barakol and related compounds, and extracts have been linked to liver injury; leaves, flowers and pods are also reported highly toxic to pigs and poultry. Avoid medicinal or animal-feed use without reliable guidance.
